scientific_question: Does defining biology after explicit inverse acquisition transport improve factor allocation relative to an exact-capacity model that has the same learned acquisition operators, paired supervision, encoder, decoder, and calibration data but encodes biology directly from the acquired observation?

motivation.v2_r1_to_r5: Peer-channel crossed factorization repeatedly retained acquisition information but showed a persistent biology-retention deficit versus matched controls.
motivation.v3r_development: After repair of an implementation-invalid orthogonal basis, inverse-transport biology passed the synthetic development gates.
motivation.v3r_confirmation: Biological recovery and known-scanner transport replicated, but incremental additive-group closure superiority over a matched nonclosed control did not.
motivation.v4_change: Remove the additive scanner-coordinate law entirely and test inverse source canonicalization itself.

generator.scanner_transform_family: Each scanner is sampled independently as a well-conditioned invertible affine feature-space acquisition transform T_s(x)=b_s+Q_s^T(exp(d_s) elementwise * Q_s x), with scanner 0 fixed to identity.
generator.heldout_scanner_calibration: After shared-model training, only scanner-5 operator parameters may be fit using 24 paired scanner-0/scanner-5 calibration identities. Calibration identities are excluded from evaluation.

architecture.scanner_operator_bank: One explicitly invertible scanner-specific affine operator per scanner; orthogonal factors computed as matrix_exp(A_s-A_s^T), diagonal positive scales exp(d_s), and translation b_s. Scanner 0 is fixed identity.
architecture.reason_scanner_id_available: v4 isolates factor-allocation structure rather than acquisition-ID inference; scanner metadata is treated as observed acquisition provenance.
architecture.only_structural_difference: Whether the source acquisition inverse T_s^-1 is applied before the shared biological encoder.

training.training_scanner_pairs: all ordered scanner pairs among scanners 0-4 for training identities

heldout_scanner_calibration.calibration_loss: paired forward and inverse operator reconstruction between scanner 0 and scanner 5

known_scanner_test: biological latent recovery R2 to true z
cross-scanner transport gain versus no transport
heldout_scanner_test_after_calibration: biological latent recovery R2 on scanner-5 test identities using a biological decoder/probe fit without scanner-5 evaluation identities
paired canonical latent alignment to scanner 0

requirements: candidate and control parameter counts exactly equal
all learned candidate and control scanner operators preserve inverse roundtrip MSE < 1e-8 on numerical probes
candidate mean heldout-scanner biological latent recovery R2 >= 0.80
candidate-minus-control heldout-scanner biological R2 has lower 95% paired-bootstrap bound > 0
control-minus-candidate heldout canonical-alignment MSE has lower 95% paired-bootstrap bound > 0
candidate-minus-control heldout same-identity retrieval has lower 95% paired-bootstrap bound >= 0
control-minus-candidate biological scanner-probe accuracy across known scanners has lower 95% paired-bootstrap bound > 0

claim_boundary: A pass would support the structural hypothesis that explicit inverse acquisition transport before biological encoding improves factor allocation under paired, provenance-known, independently generated invertible acquisition transforms with small heldout-scanner calibration. It would not establish that real scanners are exactly invertible, that scanner metadata is always available, or that additive group closure is beneficial.
stop_rule: If v4 fails the frozen promotion gate, retain the failure and do not tune on dataset seed 12037 or model seeds 4401-4405. Any successor must use a new hypothesis and fresh generator/seeds.
